items.title: Actual ideal RGO identification and normalization

source.anchor: Appendix D.1 Eq18 ideal target identification; consumed by SPHMC Appendix A.4(2)
source.attribution: ASTIS mathematical restatement and exposition of the ideal target construction used by Fan Chen, Sinho Chewi, Jianfeng Lu and Matthew S. Zhang, Smoothed Picard Hamiltonian Monte Carlo.

items.statement: exp(-f) is G-integrable with strictly positive real integral; exp(m) is q-integrable with strictly positive real integral; exp(-V) is canonical-volume-integrable with strictly positive real integral. The actual q.tilted(m) equals G.tilted(-f) and also equals volume.withDensity(x -> ofReal(exp(-V(x))/integral exp(-V) dvolume)).
assumptions: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel sigma-algebra and canonical volume. f:E->R is differentiable everywhere and its actual gradient is globally beta-Lipschitz, with beta>=0. Fix eta>0 satisfying beta*eta<1 and arbitrary x0,x_plus in E. No convexity or second differentiability is assumed.

Set g=grad f(x_plus), h=x0-eta*g, P=(z->sqrt(eta) z)_*stdGaussian(E), U=volume restricted to (0,1], nu=U product P, G=(z->x0+sqrt(eta) z)_*stdGaussian(E), and q=(z->h+sqrt(eta) z)_*stdGaussian(E). Thus time and auxiliary Gaussian inputs are independent.

For s=(r,z), theta=pi*r/2, gamma=h+sin(theta)(x-h)+cos(theta)z and v=(pi/2)(cos(theta)(x-h)-sin(theta)z). The actual untruncated estimator is W(x,s)=<v,g-grad f(gamma)>. Define m(x)=integral W(x,s) dnu(s) and V(x)=f(x)+norm(x-x0)^2/(2eta). These are definitions of actual functions and laws, not assumptions about their means or integrability.

obligations.label: Actual unclipped-mean target identification with positive finite normalization

bindings.boundary: This identifies the actual unclipped-mean ideal RGO and proves its positive finite normalization. beta*eta<1 is sufficient and contains the source Claim2 small-step range, not equivalent to all its conditions. Arbitrary reference x_plus, beta0, zero dimension and coordinate-free spaces are disclosed extensions. The public theorem has eight conclusions: three L1 statements, three positive real integrals and two measure equalities. Probability of the resulting law follows, but no separate IsProbabilityMeasure conjunct or joint adaptive-parameter kernel is returned. Clipped-vs-ideal Renyi accuracy, initialization, implementation and query costs remain separate. Neither full companion paper is complete.

assumption_deltas.source: Euclidean smooth setting in positive dimension.
assumption_deltas.lean: Finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space with canonical volume, including dimension zero.
assumption_deltas.reason: Coordinate-free Gaussian and inner-product results apply, without division by dimension.

assumption_deltas.source: The smoothness constant is conventionally positive.
assumption_deltas.lean: beta is a nonnegative real parameter (NNReal); beta=0 is allowed.
assumption_deltas.reason: No division by beta is used.

assumption_deltas.source: Claim2 uses a stronger small-step condition together with ell>=2 for clipping accuracy.
assumption_deltas.lean: eta>0 and beta*eta<1 suffice for this ideal target identification and normalization.
assumption_deltas.reason: The source smooth Claim2 range implies beta*eta<=1/(8ell)<=1/16. The ideal-only contract does not assert the clipping accuracy conclusion. Strict inequality matters: a negative quadratic can make V constant at beta*eta=1 in positive dimension.

assumption_deltas.source: A reference-point residual bound is used for downstream clipping control.
assumption_deltas.lean: x_plus is arbitrary for ideal mean identification.
assumption_deltas.reason: The likelihood cancels the affine gradient term for every reference point; the residual condition is retained for later clipping estimates.

assumption_deltas.lean: U is volume restricted to Ioc(0,1), independently multiplied by the actual auxiliary Gaussian.
assumption_deltas.reason: The endpoints are Lebesgue-null. The true path and auxiliary product are retained.

assumption_deltas.source: The ideal RGO is the normalized density proportional to exp(-V).
assumption_deltas.lean: All three required exponential weights are proved integrable with strictly positive real normalizers before identifying the measures.
assumption_deltas.reason: No assumed integrability or mean identity replaces the actual Gaussian/gradient definitions; no totalized zero denominator supplies a fake equality.

assumption_deltas.source: SPHMC A.4(2) uses the ideal construction in a terminal approximate implementation.
assumption_deltas.lean: Fixed-parameter ideal target identification only; no clipped Renyi, joint adaptive kernel, initialization or cost theorem.
assumption_deltas.reason: This is the selected dependency, not the complete implementation or full paper theorem.
